distractors.reason: We don't say 'much close'. 'Much' is used with uncountable nouns (much time) or comparatives (much better).
We don't say 'big close'. 'Big' is an adjective describing size, not a degree adverb.
We don't say 'many close'. 'Many' is used with countable plural nouns (many people), not with adjectives.

example_sentence: The bakery is ___ close to here.
l1_interference: Falantes de português podem traduzir 'muito' como 'much' ou 'big', mas com adjetivos como 'close' a forma correta é 'very'.
explanation: In English, 'very' is the normal degree adverb before most adjectives: very close, very far, very easy. Use 'much' mainly with uncountable nouns and comparatives.

related_collocations.example: The train station is very far from here.
The way to the school is very easy.
I am very tired after the long walk.

memory_tip: VERY + adjective (very close, very far) | MUCH + uncountable noun or comparative (much time, much better)
